`enum GlslDialect`<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.bridge.render.shader.source` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [GlslDialect.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/bridge/render/shader/source/GlslDialect.java)

A GLSL or GLSL ES version that the shader translator writes, with the language features that each version allows.

## Description

A backend picks one dialect for its [`GlslShaderTranslator`](/reference/pipeline/glslshadertranslator/): the translator writes the version line, the precision statements and the declarations of that dialect, and refuses a source that uses a [`ShaderFeature`](/reference/pipeline/shaderfeature/) the dialect lacks.
The shaders of JOID keep to GLSL 1.20, which every OpenGL 2.1 context compiles.

Backend note: the OpenGL backends pick the highest desktop dialect that the context reports, up to `GLSL_330`; Vulkan uses `GLSL_450`, compiled to SPIR-V.

## Learn more

- [Pick a dialect](/build/shader-translation/#pick-a-dialect)

## Methods

| Returns | Signature | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `boolean` | [supports](#GlslDialect-method-supports)(ShaderFeature feature) | If `true`, a shader in this dialect may use the feature: the version reaches its first desktop or ES version. |
| `boolean` | [hasInputOutputs](#GlslDialect-method-hasInputOutputs)() | If `true`, the dialect declares varyings with `in` and `out` and writes the color to an output (GLSL 1.30, ESSL 3.00 and later); otherwise the translator writes `attribute`, `varying`, `gl_FragColor` and `texture2D`. |
| `boolean` | [hasUniformBlocks](#GlslDialect-method-hasUniformBlocks)() | If `true`, the dialect has uniform blocks, so the translator accepts `UniformLayout.BLOCK` (GLSL 1.40, ESSL 3.00 and later). |
| `boolean` | [hasExplicitLocations](#GlslDialect-method-hasExplicitLocations)() | If `true`, the translator declares the attributes and the fragment output with `layout(location = n)` (GLSL 3.30, ESSL 3.00 and later); otherwise the backend binds the attribute locations when it links the program. |
| `boolean` | [hasImplicitConversions](#GlslDialect-method-hasImplicitConversions)() | If `true`, the compiler converts integer literals to floats where a float is expected (desktop GLSL 1.20 and later); otherwise the translator rewrites them with [`ImplicitConversion`](/reference/pipeline/implicitconversion/). |
| `String` | [getName](#GlslDialect-method-getName)() | Returns the name used in messages, such as `GLSL 3.30` or `ESSL 1.00`. |
| `String` | [getPrecision](#GlslDialect-method-getPrecision)() | Returns the precision statements written after the version line: none for desktop GLSL, `highp` for ESSL 3.00, and `highp` when the fragment stage has it, else `mediump`, for ESSL 1.00. |
| `String` | [getLineDirective](#GlslDialect-method-getLineDirective)() | Returns the `#line` directive written before the body, so that the line numbers of a compiler error are those of the source file; its value depends on how the version counts lines. |
| `int` | [getVersion](#GlslDialect-method-getVersion)() | Returns the number of the `#version` line, such as `330`. |
| `boolean` | [isEs](#GlslDialect-method-isEs)() | If `true`, the dialect is GLSL ES, for OpenGL ES and WebGL. |
| `String` | [getDeclaration](#GlslDialect-method-getDeclaration)() | Returns the `#version` line written at the top of each translated stage, such as `#version 330 core`. |

## Values

| Value | Summary |
|---|---|
| [`GLSL_110`](#GlslDialect-value-GLSL_110) | GLSL 1.10, OpenGL 2.0: no implicit conversion of integer literals. |
| [`GLSL_120`](#GlslDialect-value-GLSL_120) | GLSL 1.20, OpenGL 2.1, the version that every shader of JOID keeps to. |
| [`GLSL_130`](#GlslDialect-value-GLSL_130) | GLSL 1.30, OpenGL 3.0: `in` and `out`, `flat` varyings, unsigned integers, bitwise operators, `switch`, `texelFetch` and `textureSize`. |
| [`GLSL_140`](#GlslDialect-value-GLSL_140) | GLSL 1.40, OpenGL 3.1: uniform blocks. |
| [`GLSL_150`](#GlslDialect-value-GLSL_150) | GLSL 1.50, OpenGL 3.2. |
| [`GLSL_330`](#GlslDialect-value-GLSL_330) | GLSL 3.30 core, OpenGL 3.3: explicit locations. |
| [`GLSL_450`](#GlslDialect-value-GLSL_450) | GLSL 4.50, the dialect that the Vulkan backend compiles to SPIR-V. |
| [`ESSL_100`](#GlslDialect-value-ESSL_100) | GLSL ES 1.00, OpenGL ES 2.0 and WebGL 1. |
| [`ESSL_300`](#GlslDialect-value-ESSL_300) | GLSL ES 3.00, OpenGL ES 3.0 and WebGL 2. |

## Method details

<a id="GlslDialect-method-supports"></a>

### supports

`boolean supports(ShaderFeature feature)` 

If `true`, a shader in this dialect may use the feature: the version reaches its first desktop or ES version.

<a id="GlslDialect-method-hasInputOutputs"></a>

### hasInputOutputs

`boolean hasInputOutputs()` 

If `true`, the dialect declares varyings with `in` and `out` and writes the color to an output (GLSL 1.30, ESSL 3.00 and later); otherwise the translator writes `attribute`, `varying`, `gl_FragColor` and `texture2D`.

<a id="GlslDialect-method-hasUniformBlocks"></a>

### hasUniformBlocks

`boolean hasUniformBlocks()` 

If `true`, the dialect has uniform blocks, so the translator accepts `UniformLayout.BLOCK` (GLSL 1.40, ESSL 3.00 and later).

<a id="GlslDialect-method-hasExplicitLocations"></a>

### hasExplicitLocations

`boolean hasExplicitLocations()` 

If `true`, the translator declares the attributes and the fragment output with `layout(location = n)` (GLSL 3.30, ESSL 3.00 and later); otherwise the backend binds the attribute locations when it links the program.

<a id="GlslDialect-method-hasImplicitConversions"></a>

### hasImplicitConversions

`boolean hasImplicitConversions()` 

If `true`, the compiler converts integer literals to floats where a float is expected (desktop GLSL 1.20 and later); otherwise the translator rewrites them with [`ImplicitConversion`](/reference/pipeline/implicitconversion/).

<a id="GlslDialect-method-getName"></a>

### getName

`String getName()` 

Returns the name used in messages, such as `GLSL 3.30` or `ESSL 1.00`.

<a id="GlslDialect-method-getPrecision"></a>

### getPrecision

`String getPrecision()` 

Returns the precision statements written after the version line: none for desktop GLSL, `highp` for ESSL 3.00, and `highp` when the fragment stage has it, else `mediump`, for ESSL 1.00.

<a id="GlslDialect-method-getLineDirective"></a>

### getLineDirective

`String getLineDirective()` 

Returns the `#line` directive written before the body, so that the line numbers of a compiler error are those of the source file; its value depends on how the version counts lines.

<a id="GlslDialect-method-getVersion"></a>

### getVersion

`int getVersion()` 

Returns the number of the `#version` line, such as `330`.

<a id="GlslDialect-method-isEs"></a>

### isEs

`boolean isEs()` 

If `true`, the dialect is GLSL ES, for OpenGL ES and WebGL.

<a id="GlslDialect-method-getDeclaration"></a>

### getDeclaration

`String getDeclaration()` 

Returns the `#version` line written at the top of each translated stage, such as `#version 330 core`.
